description: CEISMIC is the Canterbury Earthquakes Digital Archive, launched by the University of Canterbury in October 2011 to collect and preserve stories, video, audio, documents and images about the 2010 and 2011 Canterbury earthquakes for commemoration, teaching and research. Its consortium includes the National Library, the Ministry for Culture and Heritage, Christchurch City Libraries, Te Papa, Canterbury Museum and the Ngāi Tahu Research Centre, and users can search across New Zealand's digital heritage collections for earthquake material. The Government's Canterbury Earthquake Recovery Learning and Legacy Programme, over 200 online items from government and non-government bodies such as the Earthquake Commission, the Red Cross and the Human Rights Commission, was transferred to CEISMIC, including copies of key documents of the Canterbury Earthquake Recovery Authority (CERA) that led the Christchurch rebuild. Coverage: Canterbury and Christchurch, New Zealand. Access: search on the CEISMIC website. Licence: varies by item and source collection; free to search. Caveats: this is a document and media archive, not a structured dataset; the DPMC pages hosting CERA plans and data returned 403 here. Simulation uses are evidence for post-earthquake recovery timelines, rebuild policy and building damage for model validation. Related records: the StEER reconnaissance record.
